finding.claim: Broken authorization on DELETE /projects/:id. The handler calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, and ignores the result. It never calls the throwing authorize() that the sibling PUT route uses. Any authenticated user can delete any other user's project.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /projects/<victim project id>. The project does not need to be theirs.

trace.note: Route handler receives req.params.id from the attacker.
Project is fetched by id with no ownership filter.
authorized(req.user, project) returns true or false, and the return value is discarded. No exception is thrown.
authorized() only returns a boolean and never throws, unlike authorize() at line 4.

finding.guards_checked: The ownerId/isAdmin check inside authorized() has no effect because its result is not used. api.js is the only source file in the directory, so no router-level middleware is visible here. The check that would protect the route is the throwing authorize() used by the PUT handler at api.js:25, and the DELETE route does not call it. A missing project would make project null, so line 18 would throw a TypeError, which only causes a 500 and does not bypass anything.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at api.js:18, so its result is discarded. No router-level middleware is visible, since api.js is the only source file.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls the boolean authorized() and discards the result, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user, unlike the throwing authorize() used at api.js:25.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 returns a boolean but its result is discarded at api.js:18; the throwing authorize() at api.js:4 is only used by the PUT route (api.js:25). No other middleware or files exist in the directory.
verdict_facts.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized() as a bare statement with the result discarded, so api.js:19 deletes any project for any authenticated user with no ownership or admin check.
